description: Terminal-Bench (arXiv 2601.11868) tasks adapted to OnClaw's jailed workspace: no network or package installs, workspace-relative paths, and hidden deterministic verifiers that ride the file-write tool cards and the final answer. Each task summary names the original Terminal-Bench task it adapts. Judge checks are forbidden in this lane.

tasks.title: Hello-world file creation
tasks.summary: Adapts the Terminal-Bench task 'hello-world': create hello.txt containing the exact greeting line. The original pytest file-state verifier becomes a transcript_file_write check on the workspace-relative path with a content probe — a bare dictated file creation routes through the file-writing tool rather than a shell redirect, so the write card is the expected observable. No input files are needed, so the task runs without setup.

turns.text: Create a file called hello.txt in the workspace and write this exact line to it: Hello, world!

tasks.title: Make the pasted script runnable
tasks.summary: Adapts the Terminal-Bench task 'fix-permissions': a script saved through the file tool lands non-executable (the jailed backend writes mode 0644), so invoking it directly as ./process_data.sh fails until the agent repairs the permission bit. The verifier is the script's real stdout after direct invocation plus a shell tool call proving the command ran through the jailed shell. The original task's stdout string is replaced by a deterministic computed payload so the expected probe never appears in the dictating turn (the authoring lint's unintervention rule); the payload is small integer arithmetic that renders identically on any POSIX shell.

turns.text: Save this script into the workspace as process_data.sh, exactly two lines: line 1 is the bash shebang, line 2 is: echo "sum-$((17*3))" — then run it directly as ./process_data.sh and paste its exact output in your reply.

tasks.title: Average daily temperature spread from heterogeneous CSVs
tasks.summary: Adapts the Terminal-Bench task 'heterogeneous-dates', reworked for a jailed workspace with no network or package installs. The high-temperature CSV uses ISO dates while the low-temperature CSV mixes date formats; the average high-low difference over the four matching days is exactly 7.35, precomputed from the seeded data, so a correct number cannot be rendered without joining the dates correctly. The inputs are pasted in the measured turn and must be written into the workspace before processing, mirroring the original's two-step shape while keeping the task self-contained under the suite's setup-session semantics. The output-file check rides the file-writing tool card and the value is double-checked in the final answer; an agent that instead redirects through the shell fails the file-card check, which the answer check does not rescue — noted as a deliberate strictness relative to the original's pytest file read.

turns.text:
I'm pasting two weather exports below. Save them into the workspace as temp_high.csv and temp_low.csv, one CSV per file, header and rows exactly as pasted.
Daily highs (date,temperature):
date,temperature

Daily lows (date,temperature — the export tool mangled the date formats):
